title: Homage to Aṅgāraka

words.gram: compound adj., m. dat. sg. (written in three parts)
words.meaning: together with the adhidevatā and the pratyadhidevatā
words.role: qualifies the graha’s name; agrees with it in case
words.context: the adhidevatā is the deity set over the graha, the pratyadhidevatā the deity set facing it; the formula names both without naming them

samasa.meaning: accompanied by the adhidevatā and the pratyadhidevatā

morphology.note: dative singular of अङ्गारक; with namaḥ the dative names the one honoured.

translation.literal: Homage to Aṅgāraka, together with the adhidevatā and the pratyadhidevatā.
translation.readable: Homage to Aṅgāraka and to the deities who attend him.

sandhi_exceptions.note: The witness writes सहिताय अङ्गारकाय with the vowels apart (-a ā-/-a a-), the formula being said as separate words; joined they would merge.

meaning: The salutation that closes each graha’s part of the sūktam: homage to Aṅgāraka — Mars, ‘the glowing coal’ — together with the adhidevatā and the pratyadhidevatā, the two deities associated with the graha. The formula names them together and does not say who they are; nor does the witness say which of the graha’s three mantras is addressed to which. The dative अङ्गारकाय names the one honoured; namaḥ, ‘homage’, is the whole of the act.
in_the_rite: Step 2 (Aṅgāraka), after Aṅgāraka’s three mantras (agnir mūrdhā, syonā pṛthivi, kṣetrasya patinā). The same formula ends each of the nine steps, with the graha’s name in the dative.

notes.label: linguistic
notes.text: The witness writes the compound in three parts (अधिदेवता प्रत्यधिदेवता सहिताय); grammatically it is one word, agreeing in case with the graha’s name. The svara marks on the last two words are the witness’s.
